The '''78th Primetime Emmy Awards''' honored the best in American [[prime time]] television programming from June{{nbsp}}1, 2025, until May{{nbsp}}31, 2026, as chosen by the [[Academy of Television Arts & Sciences]].<ref>{{cite press release |url=https://www.televisionacademy.com/files/assets/Downloads/2026-rules-procedures-v4.pdf |title=78th Emmy Awards – 2025–2026 Rules and Procedures |date=April 7, 2026 |publisher=[[Academy of Television Arts & Sciences]] |access-date=May 11, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260708184053/https://www.televisionacademy.com/files/assets/Downloads/2026-rules-procedures-v4.pdf |archive-date=July 8, 2026 }}</ref>   The awards ceremony was held live on September{{nbsp}}14, 2026, at the [[Peacock Theater]] in [[Downtown Los Angeles]], California, and was preceded by the [[78th Primetime Creative Arts Emmy Awards|78th{{nbsp}}Primetime Creative Arts Emmy Awards]] on September{{nbsp}}5 and{{nbsp}}6. The ceremony was produced by Jesse Collins Entertainment and broadcast in the United States by [[NBC]] and [[Peacock (streaming service)|Peacock]].<ref name="Airdate">{{cite web |url=https://deadline.com/2025/11/2026-emmys-airdate-nbc-1236621428/ |title=2026 Emmys Gets Airdate on NBC |last=Petski |first=Denise |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |date=November 18, 2025 |access-date=March 3, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nbc.com/nbc-insider/2026-emmys-air-date-announcement |title=NBC Reveals the Air Date for the 78th Emmy Awards in 2026 |last=Phelan |first=Chris |publisher=[[NBC]] |date=November 18, 2025 |access-date=March 3, 2026}}</ref><ref name="Calendar">{{cite web |url=https://variety.com/2025/tv/news/emmy-calendar-2026-voting-nomination-dates-tv-academy-1236607719/ |title=TV Academy Reveals Emmy Calendar for 2026 — Including Eligibility, Submission, Voting, and Nomination Dates |last=Schneider |first=Michael |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |date=December 12, 2025 |access-date=March 3, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://deadline.com/2026/04/jesse-collins-entertainment-emmys-2-1236876445/ |title=Jesse Collins Entertainment to Produce Emmys, Again |last=White |first=Peter |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |date=April 30, 2026 |access-date=May 1, 2026}}</ref> The ceremony was produced by Jesse Collins Entertainment, directed by Alex Rudzinski, and broadcast in the United States by [[NBC]] and [[Peacock (streaming service)|Peacock]]. [[Mariska Hargitay]] hosted the event.<ref name="Hargitay"/>

At the main ceremony, ''[[Widow's Bay]]'' led all programs with six awards including [[Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Comedy Series|Outstanding Comedy Series]], and ''[[The Pitt]]'' won two awards including [[Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Drama Series|Outstanding Drama Series]]. Other winning programs included ''[[Pluribus (TV series)|Pluribus]]'' with two awards, and ''[[The Beast in Me (TV series)|The Beast in Me]]'', ''[[DTF St. Louis]]'', ''[[Hacks]]'', ''[[The Late Show with Stephen Colbert]]'', ''[[Remarkably Bright Creatures (film)|Remarkably Bright Creatures]]'', ''[[Slow Horses]]'', and ''[[The Traitors (American TV series)|The Traitors]]'' with one each. Including Creative Arts Emmys, ''Widow's Bay'' led all shows with 14 wins, while [[Apple TV (streaming service)|Apple TV]] led all networks with 28 wins.

The nominations for the 78th Primetime Emmy Awards were announced on July 8, 2026, at the Television Academy's Wolf Theatre in [[North Hollywood, Los Angeles]], hosted by actor [[Jeff Hiller]] and actress [[Liza Colón-Zayas]], along with Television Academy chair [[Cris Abrego]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Loving |first1=Casey |title=How to Watch the 2026 Emmy Nominations Live |url=https://www.thewrap.com/industry-news/awards/how-to-watch-emmy-nominations-live-2026/ |access-date=July 15, 2026 |work=[[TheWrap]] |date=July 8, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260709031609/https://www.thewrap.com/industry-news/awards/how-to-watch-emmy-nominations-live-2026/ |archive-date=July 9, 2026 |language=en-US |url-status=live}}</ref> Including nominations at the [[78th Primetime Creative Arts Emmy Awards]], ''[[The Pitt]]'' led all programs with 25 nominations, followed by ''[[Hacks]]'' with 24 nominations.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Dalton |first1=Andrew |title=''The Pitt'' Leads with 25 Emmy Nominations; ''Hacks'' Breaks Record for Comedies with 24 |url=https://apnews.com/article/emmy-nominations-pluribus-beef-hacks-pitt-7d21700a43d7d5da1a662898e3646d46 |access-date=August 11, 2006 |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=July 8, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260708150816/https://apnews.com/article/emmy-nominations-pluribus-beef-hacks-pitt-7d21700a43d7d5da1a662898e3646d46 |archive-date=July 8, 2026 |language=en-US |url-status=live}}</ref> ''Hacks'' became the most-nominated comedy series for a single season in the awards' history with 24 nominations; the program surpassed the record jointly held by the [[FX (TV channel)|FX]] comedy-drama series ''[[The Bear (TV series)|The Bear]]'' and the [[Apple TV (streaming service)|Apple TV]] comedy series ''[[The Studio (TV series)|The Studio]]'' which earned 23 nominations in [[76th Primetime Emmy Awards|2024]] and [[77th Primetime Emmy Awards|2025]], respectively.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Porter |first1=Rick |title=''Hacks'' Creators on Their Record-Breaking Emmy Nomination Haul: 'Incredible Way to End' |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-features/hacks-creators-record-breaking-emmy-nominations-1236642225/ |access-date=August 11, 2026 |work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |date=July 8, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260709200649/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-features/hacks-creators-record-breaking-emmy-nominations-1236642225/ |archive-date=July 9, 2026 |language=en-US |url-status=live}}</ref> [[HBO]] and its streaming service [[HBO Max]] led all networks and platforms with 123 nominations; [[Netflix]] came in second place with 109 nominations.

Winners are listed first, highlighted in '''boldface''', and indicated with a double dagger (‡).<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-09-15 |title=Emmys 2026: The winners in full |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/ce8l9pnkn62o |access-date=2026-09-15 |publisher=[[BBC]] |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Gonzalez |first=Shivani |date=2026-09-14 |title=Emmy Awards Winners 2026: See the Full List |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/09/14/arts/television/emmy-winners-list.html |access-date=2026-09-15 |work=[[The New York Times]] |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref>{{efn |The outlets listed for each program are the U.S. broadcasters or streaming services identified in the nominations, which for some international productions are different than the broadcaster(s) that originally commissioned the program. Programs broadcast by [[HBO]] or [[HBO Max]] were listed under both services in the nominations list; only the original broadcaster is listed below.}} For simplicity, producers who received nominations for program awards have been omitted.

===Bob Hope Humanitarian Award===
The [[Bob Hope Humanitarian Award]] was presented to actor and activist [[Michael J. Fox]], in recognition of "his transformative contributions to [[Parkinson's disease]] research and advocacy".<ref>{{cite web |url=https://variety.com/2026/tv/news/michael-j-fox-bob-hope-humanitarian-award-emmys-1236823047/ |title=Michael J. Fox Will Be Honored with TV Academy's Bob Hope Humanitarian Award at the Emmys |last=Schneider |first=Michael |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |date=July 29, 2026 |access-date=July 30, 2026}}</ref>

===Multiple nominations and wins===
For the purposes of the lists below, "major" constitutes the categories listed above (program, acting, directing, and writing), while "total" includes the categories presented at the [[78th Primetime Creative Arts Emmy Awards|Creative Arts Emmy Awards ceremony]]. Programs and networks must have multiple wins or major nominations or at least five total nominations to be included.

==Ceremony information==
[[File:Mariska Hargitay Woodstock Film Festival.jpg|right|thumb|upright|alt=Mariska Hargitay in 2025.|[[Mariska Hargitay]] hosted the ceremony.]]

The nominations for the 78th{{nbsp}}Primetime Emmy Awards were announced on July{{nbsp}}8, 2026, at the Television Academy's Wolf Theatre in [[North Hollywood, Los Angeles]], hosted by actor [[Jeff Hiller]] and actress [[Liza Colón-Zayas]], along with Television Academy chair [[Cris Abrego]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.televisionacademy.com/features/news/awards-news/260618-emmy-nominations-announcement |title=Emmy Winners Liza Colón-Zayas and Jeff Hiller to Announce 78th Emmy Awards Nominations July 8 |publisher=[[Academy of Television Arts & Sciences]] |date=June 18, 2026 |access-date=June 18, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-news/watch-2026-emmy-nominations-livestream-online-1236640358/ |title=2026 Emmy Nominations: Watch the Livestream |last=Jeffries |first=Naomi |website=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |date=July 8, 2026 |access-date=July 8, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://deadline.com/lists/emmy-nominations-full-list-nominees-scorecard/ |title=Emmy Nominations 2026: The Complete List |last1=Gomez |first1=Dessi |last2=Hipes |first2=Patrick |last3=Pedersen |first3=Erik |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |date=July 8, 2026 |access-date=July 8, 2026}}</ref> The nominations for [[Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Variety Series|Outstanding Variety Series]] and [[Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Reality Competition Program|Outstanding Reality Competition Program]] were announced three hours before the rest of the categories.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://deadline.com/2026/07/colbert-kimmel-john-oliver-jon-stewart-snl-late-night-emmys-1236975168/ |title=Stephen Colbert, Jimmy Kimmel, John Oliver, Jon Stewart & 'SNL' to Battle It Out for Bumper Late-Night Emmy or Emmys |last=White |first=Peter |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |date=July 8, 2026 |access-date=July 8, 2026}}</ref> On July{{nbsp}}7, actress [[Mariska Hargitay]] was announced as the ceremony's host.<ref name="Hargitay">{{cite web |url=https://deadline.com/2026/07/mariska-hargitay-host-2026-emmy-awards-nbc-1236975778/ |title=Mariska Hargitay to Host 2026 Emmy Awards on NBC |last=Andreeva |first=Nellie |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |date=July 7, 2026 |access-date=July 7, 2026}}</ref> [[NBC]] and the [[Academy of Television Arts & Sciences|Television Academy]] considered talent both within and outside of [[NBCUniversal]] for the role, but ultimately hired NBC's ''[[Law & Order: Special Victims Unit]]''{{'}}s lead actress in honor of the network's 100th{{nbsp}}anniversary. This was the first Primetime Emmys ceremony that the host is not a comedian, comedy performer, reality host or television personality since [[Angela Lansbury]] in [[45th Primetime Emmy Awards|1993]], and the first time that the event was hosted by a woman since [[Jane Lynch]] in [[63rd Primetime Emmy Awards|2011]].<ref name="Hargitay"/>

Jesse Collins, Dionne Harmon, and Jeannae Rouzan-Clay of Jesse Collins Entertainment  served as [[executive producer]]s of the telecast.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.televisionacademy.com/features/news/awards-news/260707-78th-emmys-host-mariska-hargitay |title=Mariska Hargitay to Host 78th Emmy Awards on NBC |publisher=[[Academy of Television Arts & Sciences]] |date=July 7, 2026 |access-date=July 7, 2026}}</ref> To avoid conflicts with the network's broadcast of ''[[NBC Sunday Night Football]]'', the event was scheduled on a Monday night, instead of a Sunday, which NBC had previously done when they aired the awards ceremony every four years since 2014.<ref name="Airdate"/>

===Category and rule changes===
In January{{nbsp}}2026, the Television Academy announced plans to present its first new major award in nearly twenty years with the creation of the Legacy Award, which will be presented annually to television programs that have made a "profound and lasting impact" on audiences, and remain relevant to culture, society and the industry.<ref>{{cite press release |url=https://www.televisionacademy.com/features/news/awards-news/2026-legacy-award-260108 |title=Television Academy Announces Plans for First New Major Award in Nearly 20 Years |publisher=[[Academy of Television Arts & Sciences]] |date=January 8, 2026 |access-date=March 3, 2026}}</ref> Additionally, [[Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Scripted Variety Series|Outstanding Scripted Variety Series]] and [[Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Talk Series|Outstanding Talk Series]] were merged into Outstanding Variety Series. The new Variety Series category is tracked, meaning the number of nominees from each format is proportional to the number of submissions, and it became an area award where voters select any and all nominees they believe deserve an award, with the potential for multiple winners.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.televisionacademy.com/features/news/awards-news/260128-emmys-variety-rules |title=Emmys Rules Merge Variety Categories |publisher=[[Academy of Television Arts & Sciences]] |date=January 28, 2026 |access-date=July 8, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.indiewire.com/awards/industry/2026-emmys-rule-changes-good-bad-basic-1235186297/ |title=The Good, the Bad, and the Basic Rule Changes Affecting the 2026 Emmys |last=Jones |first=Marcus |website=[[IndieWire]] |date=March 26, 2026 |access-date=July 23, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://variety.com/lists/2026-emmys-best-variety-series-predictions/1236757434/ |title=Emmys: Outstanding Variety Series — The New Rules That Could Produce Five Winners |last=Davis |first=Clayton |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |date=July 1, 2026 |access-date=July 23, 2026}}</ref>

In July, the Television Academy voted to move five categories to the Creative Arts ceremonies on the preceding weekend: [[Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Supporting Actor in a Limited or Anthology Series or Movie|Outstanding Supporting Actor]], [[Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Supporting Actress in a Limited or Anthology Series or Movie|Supporting Actress]], [[Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Directing for a Limited or Anthology Series or Movie|Directing]], and [[Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Writing for a Limited or Anthology Series or Movie|Writing for a Limited or Anthology Series or Movie]] and [[Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Writing for a Variety Series|Writing for a Variety Series]]. Abrego justified the changes as a way to add other elements to the show such as musical performances or comedy segments, with the moves selected to "be as balanced and as equitable as possible".<ref>{{cite web |url=https://variety.com/2026/tv/news/emmys-removes-categories-telecast-supporting-limited-acting-1236814429/ |title=Emmys to Move Five Categories Out of NBC Telecast in a Bid to Revamp the Ceremony (Exclusive) |last=Schneider |first=Michael |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |date=July 17, 2026 |access-date=July 23, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.televisionacademy.com/features/news/awards-news/260717-78th-emmys-categories-by-show |title=Emmys Update — Categories by Show |publisher=[[Academy of Television Arts & Sciences]] |date=July 17, 2026 |access-date=July 23, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://deadline.com/2026/07/emmys-cuts-televised-categories-2026-ceremony-1236997119/ |title=Emmys Cuts Number of Televised Categories for 2026 Primetime Ceremony |last=White |first=Peter |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |date=July 17, 2026 |access-date=July 23, 2026}}</ref> A joint statement from the [[Directors Guild of America]], the [[Writers Guild of America]], and [[SAG-AFTRA]] criticized the changes and commented, "The decision to eliminate these categories from the prime-time broadcast devalues the contributions of the talented people the Academy is meant to honor."<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.wga.org/news-events/news/press/2026/statement-on-emmys-broadcast-changes |title=Statement on Emmys Broadcast Changes |publisher=[[Writers Guild of America West]] |date=July 17, 2026 |access-date=July 23, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.indiewire.com/awards/industry/will-2026-emmys-bring-back-cut-categories-1235206508/ |title=Will the Emmys Bring Back Cut Categories? History Provides Hope |last=Jones |first=Marcus |website=[[IndieWire]] |date=July 21, 2026 |access-date=July 23, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://variety.com/2026/tv/columns/emmys-shake-up-telecast-move-categories-tv-academy-trying-1236819841/ |title=Shaking Up the Emmys By Moving Five Categories Out of the Telecast Might Not Work, But at Least the TV Academy is Trying Something |last=Schneider |first=Michael |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |date=July 23, 2026 |access-date=July 23, 2026}}</ref> "The move doesn't make much sense. All they've done is piss off a lot of the people and stars they are trying to court and attend their ceremony. I think this will blow up in their face", one outraged awards strategist told ''[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]''.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://variety.com/2026/tv/columns/emmys-cut-five-categories-telecast-backlash-1236816847/ |title=The Emmys 'F—ed This Up': Streamers and Networks Are Outraged as Five Categories Get Cut from the Telecast |last=Davis |first=Clayton |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |date=July 20, 2026 |access-date=July 25, 2026}}</ref> Additionally, [[Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Variety Special (Live)|Outstanding Variety Special (Live)]] was shifted back to the Creative Arts ceremonies, leaving 19{{nbsp}}categories for the main ceremony (a decrease from last year's 26).<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.thewrap.com/industry-news/awards/television-academy-cuts-7-categories-primetime-emmys/ |title=Television Academy Cuts 7 Categories from 2026 Primetime Emmys Telecast |last=Loving |first=Casey |website=[[TheWrap]] |date=July 17, 2026 |access-date=July 23, 2026}}</ref>

==In Memoriam==
The In Memoriam segment was presented by [[Macaulay Culkin]], [[Annie Murphy]] and [[Dan Levy (Canadian actor)|Dan Levy]], and featured [[Noah Kahan]] singing "[[Bridge over Troubled Water (song)|Bridge Over Troubled Water]]".<ref>{{cite magazine |first=P. Claire |last=Dodson |title=Noah Kahan Performs Heartbreaking 'In Memoriam' at Emmys 2026: Watch ‘Bridge Over Troubled Water’ |magazine=[[Teen Vogue]] |date=2026-09-14 |url=https://www.teenvogue.com/story/noah-kahan-in-memoriam-emmys-2026-09-14 |access-date=2026-09-14}}</ref><ref>{{cite AV media |title=In Memoriam: 78th Emmy Awards |publisher=[[Academy of Television Arts & Sciences]] |medium=[[YouTube]] |location=[[Los Angeles]] |date=2026-09-14 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cOxmrVZr5WQ |access-date=2026-09-15}}</ref>

* [[James Burrows]] {{endash}} director
* [[Rob Reiner]] {{endash}} performer, producer, writer
}}

Earlier in the show, Parton was honored by [[Sally Field]], with [[Reba McEntire]] performing Parton's song "Appalachian Memories". At the beginning of the tribute, O'Hara was eulogized by Culkin, Murphy, and Levy. To close the segment,  Burrows and Reiner were honored by [[Jamie Lee Curtis]].
